# Voice & Publish Editor Insight

The README first screen is stronger when it leads with Thor's name, identifies the readers, and states what they can use before it explains the repository stack. Direct first-person language keeps that framing personal: Thor shares practical lessons for technology and security leaders, builders, and people growing their careers, while the site gives him an owned place to keep his writing and resume current.

Keep the repository paths and publishing reminders as concise reference material below that opening. Agent workflow belongs in the repository instructions, not in the human-facing README.
